function: Joint DRL control of device transmit power, CPU frequency, UAV trajectory and offloading to maximize secure computation capacity versus energy against an aerial eavesdropper (p. 6)
system: NOMA uplink, 5 ground devices to a rotary-wing UAV server, jammer, aerial eavesdropper; no RIS; antenna count and band not stated (p. 3, 10)
method: DNN with order-preserving quantization (DNOP) for binary offloading plus double deep Q-network for power, frequency, trajectory; online reinforcement learning from interaction (p. 6-9)
data_channel: Own simulator: LoS free-space path loss h = beta0/d^2, 5 random devices, fixed-altitude UAVs; no dataset, trained online in the same simulator (p. 3, 10)
test_conditions: Trained and evaluated in the same simulated setup; results sweep CPU cycles per bit, local bits, maximum UAV frequency, attack power; no unseen scenario (p. 11-12)
baselines: Learned: DDQN with TDMA offloading [31] (Scheme 1). Non-learned: iterative algorithm with traditional transmission [37] (Scheme 2). Ablation: DRCTORA without power allocation (Scheme 3) (p. 13)
metrics: Secure transmission effectiveness (objective), secure computation capacity, weighted energy consumption, reward convergence, and optimized UAV trajectory (p. 10-13)
complexity: Order O(E N Z sum xi_(g-1) xi_g) for DRCTORA, O(sum xi_(g-1) xi_g) per DDQN execution; no runtime or FLOPs (p. 10)
q1_support: p. 3: "as LoS channels, which are modeled as free-space pathloss"; custom simulator, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "there are five devices and one LJ randomly" placed in one simulated area; p. 11: "Fig. 6 depicts the system performance of DRCTORA" versus CPU cycles, a parameter sweep of the same simulator; no unseen scenario or adaptation reported.
q3_support: p. 13: "variables are optimized based on DDQN [31]" (earlier learned method of the same authors, Scheme 1); p. 13: "optimized based on the iterative" algorithm [37] (non-learned, Scheme 2); Fig. 9 compares secure transmission effectiveness with both.
q4_support: p. 10: "In the DRCTORA scheme, the complexity is primarily" generated by Algorithms 2 and 3; Section IV-B gives O(E N Z sum xi_(g-1) xi_g) for Algorithm 1.
q5_support: p. 10: "there are five devices and one LJ randomly" placed in the paper's own simulation; no public dataset and no code or data link anywhere in the paper.
notes: Borderline eligibility (above_phy and function). The DDQN picks device transmit power (physical layer, aerial link) jointly with CPU frequency and UAV trajectory (p. 8 defines its action this way) and the DNN picks task offloading (above the physical layer). Kept under the rule that a learned physical-layer decision taken jointly with one above it passes above_phy, area 6 as power and resource control of a UAV link; reviewer should confirm. Scheme 3 is an ablation and is not counted for q3. Fig. 9 is plotted against bandwidth B (p. 13). The complexity formula was read from the page image of p. 10.
